craft_notes: Sthāyin: adbhuta of priceless taste; vyabhicāri vismaya at melted-rule sweetness. Sanskrit-first: aviruddhair (UNOPPOSED per SD over print viruddhair — sense-requires, recorded); amūlya (PAST-PRICE — kept priceless). Rows: 1 (‘past price’ closes — pricelessness last), 9 (unpartitioned/unopposed pair). Close: ‘knowing supreme, past price’. Rupture: comma (taste turns to flood — what taste, then how much). Rejected: print viruddhair — killed: sense requires (recorded); ‘boundless’ for unpartitioned — killed: akhaṇḍa kept (unpartitioned technical). Read aloud: WHERE be-GIN-nings VA-ry AND-rules HAVE-melt-ed, WHAT-taste IS-there, un-par-TI-tioned … FLOODS un-op-POSED, KNOW-ing su-PREME, past-PRICE.

lines: Where beginnings vary and rules have melted, what taste is there, unpartitioned,
full past compare? Self's light-yoke is one with all that is; floods unopposed, knowing supreme, past price.
l4.sanskrit_cite: vicitrārambhatve galitaniyame yaḥ kila rasaḥ | sakalabhavabhāvaikamayatāviruddhair dharmaughaiḥ paracitir anarghocitaguṇā

reads_against.argmap: What taste has the beginningless? → Partitionless taste, unopposed floods: supreme knowing priceless.
c1_essence: Unpartitioned taste, unopposed floods, priceless knowing.
